letters.title: Welcome to the valley
letters.text: Ilse's farm has a keeper again! I keep the store lit for whoever comes back, and today that's you. The town board posts requests and little jobs every morning. Here are some seeds to get you going.

letters.title: Your first harvest!
letters.text: I saw your first crops come in. Fertilizer on tilled soil makes silver and gold ones more likely. Have a few on me.

letters.title: First green
letters.text: First green this valley's seen in years. Ilse said the soil remembers. She left this for whoever came. Her journal was in the tin. Read the first page.

letters.title: A fellow angler
letters.text: Word travels fast: you landed a fish! Bait makes them bite sooner. Rainy days bring out the catfish.

letters.title: About that ore
letters.text: Copper and iron turn into bars in a furnace. Tool upgrades at the store need bars. Keep swinging!

letters.title: Summer stock is in
letters.text: Tomato, melon and corn seeds are on the shelf. Corn keeps giving after the first harvest. Crops wither when their season ends, so plan ahead.

letters.title: Fall stock is in
letters.text: Pumpkin and yam seeds are on the shelf. Pumpkins are the best money in the valley, if you have the land.

letters.title: Winter on the farm
letters.text: Only kale grows in the cold. It is a good season to mine, fish, fill the jars and fund a town project.

letters.title: A town fund
letters.text: The town is saving up for a roof over the board, a library and more. Any gold you can spare helps. Look for Town projects on the board.

letters.title: Thank you, neighbour
letters.text: You always stop to chat. It means a lot out here. These are from my own trees.

letters.title: A spot by the lake
letters.text: Most folks find the lake boring. Not you. Here is my best bait. Do not tell anyone.

letters.title: From the shop
letters.text: You are my best customer, and a good friend. A little something from the back room.

letters.title: Spare bars
letters.text: Had a few bars left over after a big job. They are better on your tools than on my shelf.

letters.title: Nothing personal
letters.text: I've fed this town alone seven years. Board requests left to their last day are mine at 2 PM. Crops, eggs and what you make of them count; fish and wild goods don't. I ship a crate a week, more often while you lead. Beat me in a season: 300¤ and a trophy for your house.

letters.title: Mind the crows
letters.text: Crows come down to the fields after the first week. A scarecrow keeps them off the crops around it. Here, take my spare one!

letters.title: Legends of the valley
letters.text: Four giant fish live here, one a season, and each bites only once. A trout in the town river on rainy spring days, once the river's back. A golden carp in your own pond in summer. Old Whiskers in the woods when fall rain falls. A pike under the winter ice in town, river willing.

letters.title: A sack at the gate
letters.text: For the field by the creek. Don't make a fuss about it.

letters.title: The gorge
letters.text: I walked up to the gorge today. It's only stones, and stones can be moved. Orin can make a sluice gate for the gap. Meet me at the weir?

letters.title: Drift timber
letters.text: The river's bringing timber down from the hills. I've made you a hook on a rope for it, 250¤. Hook a log from the bank, walk it to the slip on the south bank. Houses want timber.

letters.title: Our old house
letters.text: Mara writes that someone is mending our house, with timber out of the river. I didn't dare believe it. If the wheel can turn again, I'm coming home.

letters.title: Picky fish
letters.text: The fish won't take a bare hook any more: every cast needs bait now. I put 10 worms in your bag. The hoe digs up more, and Mara sells Bait Mix.

letters.title: Worms for you
letters.text: Your bag was too full for the worms I meant to give you, so here they are. Every cast takes one bait.

letters.title: The ledger
letters.text: I keep a ledger of every family that left: where they went, what they grew. Since you came, I've started writing to them again. A few bulbs from the back shelf.

letters.title: The Heron
letters.text: My father's boat still sits on the mud where the river was. Some evenings I sit in her and listen. Don't tell Mara. Worms, for your hook.

letters.title: Ilse's hands
letters.text: You hold a hoe the way Ilse did, low and patient. She'd be glad. She always put parsnips in first. So should you.

letters.title: A cold forge
letters.text: The wheel that worked my bellows stopped when the river left. A cold forge still mends hinges. Stone for your paths.

letters.title: Hm.
letters.text: Didn't think you'd last the month. You might. Here. Don't get used to it.

letters.title: Flour dust
letters.text: The mill still smells of old flour. When the wheel turns I'll bake for the whole valley. That's a promise.

letters.title: My brother
letters.text: Told my brother about you. He laughed. Then he asked if you needed a hand. Seeds from my own row.

letters.title: First bake
letters.text: First tart out of the old oven. It came out lopsided. It's yours anyway.

letters.title: Ilse's notes
letters.text: Ilse kept notes on how a farm pays its way. I copied the useful bits into a Guide for you: Menu, then Book. Gold first, then crops.

letters.title: Getting to know folks
letters.text: Folks here warm up slowly! A chat a day helps, and a gift they love helps more. Every heart brings something: my sheet tells you what's next.

letters.title: Practice
letters.text: Hands learn. Every harvest, cast and swing teaches you something. Menu, then Skill, shows where you stand.

letters.title: A workbench
letters.text: You'll want bait, fertilizer, sprinklers. Menu, then Make. Fiber comes from weeds and dry grass. Here's a start.

letters.title: Bait
letters.text: Fish won't take a bare hook. The hoe digs up worms. Mara sells Bait Mix. Mornings bite best.

letters.title: The mine
letters.text: Past the woods there's a mine. Rocks give stone, veins give ore. Bring a pickaxe and something to eat.

letters.title: Let the farm work
letters.text: A sprinkler waters while you sleep. A jar turns fruit into jam worth more. Both are made from fiber: Menu, then Make.

letters.title: Hens in stock
letters.text: I've chickens in stock now! Build a coop first (Menu, then Make), then come and see me. Eggs every morning!

letters.title: Home cooking
letters.text: A kitchen (the Home tab at my shop) lets you cook. A good dish gives you energy back, and some folks love one!
